P1.evidence: Setter notes were read back repeatedly and used to open threads — 'Kyla mentioned that you are pretty busy at the moment, like covering for your boss', 'Kaila also mentioned that you have or went through scoliosis' — and the rep framed why he was re-asking: 'Kyla gave me a good context of your situation, but I'm kind of old school. I want to hear it directly from the person.' The frame itself was three-part rather than four: 'to understand where you're at and where you're actually trying to build. And then I'll show you exactly how we approach that for you specifically ... we can talk about next steps' — no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement taken ('If that makes sense' / 'Sounds good') and a clean open question followed.

P2.evidence: Injuries were worked properly, including duration — 'can you put a date? How long have you been feeling that?' produced 'easily, five years'. Work and sitting were asked directly, and sleep and energy were both probed off the stress thread. Height, weight and current age were volunteered rather than asked; the only age question was about the past growth spurt. Health conditions were only reached because the setter had flagged scoliosis; there was no open conditions or hereditary question. Diet emerged during the nutrition pillar rather than at baseline, and the training week emerged in fragments.

P3.evidence: The strongest goals work in the batch. The bridge ran almost verbatim — 'why that matters to you, like of course beyond the physical appearance, what does feeling and moving that way, what would it give you?' — producing 'Confidence.' The rep then refused to accept the label and drilled it: 'Explain to me what confidence actually means to you', then 'what does that voice say to you', then reframed the prospect's own past win into a second voice, 'so what was the angel saying to you that you actually pushed through'. Identity was reached ('you're a man, you can move stuff around') and the reflect-back landed twice. The one gap is that 'who else does that impact' was never asked — everything stayed inside the prospect, and no family, partner or legacy stake was ever attached to the decision.

P4.evidence: Every prior attempt was surfaced — Move Method, the ATG/knees-over-toes app and coaching, calisthenics, martial arts and the failed PT — and the failure was fully excavated: 'What went wrong, sorry. What was the bad experience that you had?' The prospect named the structural gap himself: the Move Method 'runs the same sequence for everyone' and has 'nothing on the upper body'. The rep diagnosed the need rather than asking for it ('what you need is someone who looks at your body ... not a generic kind of thing'), which is why P4d is partial. P4f is marked N/A because its premise does not hold for this prospect — he demonstrably does stick to things on his own for years at a time.

P5.evidence: Not run at all. The rep asked the mirror-image question instead — 'let's imagine six months from now ... what would be the ideal situation' — and never asked what two more years of the same looks like. This is the decisive failure of the call: the prospect had already handed over the material ('I find it very, very painful to think that I would get older without having tried') and had explicitly said his window for adding muscle is closing, and none of it was turned back on a three-month delay. Nothing resembling 'is that something you're willing to settle for' or 'are you ready to draw a line in the sand' was said.

P6.evidence: P6a ran before the price and again after: 'if you had the right training, nutrition, and accountability all built around your life, you would be set to go' and later 'aside the money part, do you feel confident that working with Trevor would actually get you to your goals?' The answer was 'Possibly, yes.' The rep pushed once — 'Only possibly?' — got a clear no-belief explanation, and then advanced to the trial offer anyway. That is the exact instruction P6c exists to prevent: hesitation surfaced and the rep did not return to Phase 5. The 1-10 scale was used as the isolation variant and returned an 8, but the follow-up 'what would need to happen to make it a 10' was answered with a joke and never re-asked seriously.

P11.evidence: No agreement and no payment; the call ended with a calendar booking three and a half months out, so none of the payment or onboarding steps were reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest OE trigger in the batch and not one move ran. The prospect gave the play its own premise: 'I've got burned very badly once, and it took me a long time to recover from that, to even trust people', and then 'I haven't tasted the method in any way ... until I can do that, I can't say it's true or yes or no'. The script has a purpose-built response for precisely this — 'BURNED BEFORE: if you got hurt in a relationship once, do you never trust again?' — plus the certainty question, the bridge and the plane. None was used. The rep instead validated the position and sold a paid trial around it.

Trigger was explicit and repeated: 'I would only do that in September because I want to finish my current', 'I don't have time', 'for the next three months, at least'. The rep made one attempt — 'why postponing that when you could actually combine that and supplement what you're doing' and 'waiting three months, that doesn't add up for me' — which is closest to the OD logic but was abandoned the moment the prospect pushed back. None of 'things never slow down', 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled', or 'the only thing you can control is right now' was used, despite the prospect having just said his muscle-building window is closing with age.

No money objection at any point. $6,000 was received with 'Okay, okay. So that would be in September, $6,000, right?' The only money-adjacent statement was a commitment principle, not an affordability one: 'I will not put the money down until I started doing it.'

Programme-before-coaching objection, with no scripted play. The prospect stated a repeatable personal buying rule — six to eight months on a provider's programme, then coaching if satisfied — and said it has worked several times. The script has no path for staging a buyer through a lower-tier product, and critically the rep never mentioned Primal University even though the setter had already told the prospect a separate non-coaching programme exists ('Karila did mention that ... you guys also have a separate program and not just a coaching program, so I'm curious about both sides'). The prospect asked, twice, for the product that was never named.

notes: Textbook discovery through Phase 4 and a genuinely skilled emotional excavation in Phase 3, then the call fell off a cliff: no consequence frame, a 'possibly' waved through at the commitment check, and a three-and-a-half-month delay accepted after a single challenge. The one coaching instruction is to run Phase 5 on the delay itself — this prospect handed over an ageing-window fear and a fear of regret and neither was ever pointed at September.
